literal: Again, while holding his original office he was assigned to administer Zhengzhou affairs; before he set out, a household retainer reported that Bi was plotting rebellion. He was arrested and imprisoned; the investigation found no substance, and only after a long time was he pardoned.
idiomatic: Again, while still in his original post, he was ordered to handle affairs at Zhengzhou. Before he set out, a household retainer accused him of plotting rebellion. He was arrested and jailed; the inquiry found nothing, and only after a long while was he forgiven.

literal: Because of this he ceased attending court.
idiomatic: After that he stopped coming to court.

literal: He was again punished because his second son Taiqing, as supervisory official of the Court of the Imperial Clan, was slow in handling cases, and he and the court officials were all sued by Langzhong Feng Jingzhe.
idiomatic: He was punished again when his second son Taiqing, as supervisory official of the court of the imperial clan, was slow in deciding cases, and he and the court officials were all impeached by langzhong Feng Jingzhe.

literal: When the matter reached the emperor's ears, Xianzu flew into a rage and transferred Bi to Linhai garrison.
idiomatic: When the matter reached the throne, Gao Yang flew into a rage and transferred Bi to Linhai garrison.

literal: At that time Bai'e of Chuzhou plotted rebellion with north-south response; Linhai garrison was attacked by bandit leaders Zhang Chuo, Pan Tianhe, and others. Bi led and encouraged the townspeople and finally held the place secure.
idiomatic: At that time Dongfang Bai'e of Chuzhou rose in rebellion with echoes north and south. Linhai garrison was attacked by bandit leaders Zhang Chuo, Pan Tianhe, and others. Bi rallied the townspeople and in the end held the place secure.

literal: Xianzu praised this and ordered him to administer Haizhou affairs — the very province to which he had been transferred.
idiomatic: Gao Yang praised this and ordered him to administer Haizhou — the very province to which he had been sent.

literal: In the province he memorialized concerning Tongling road and the old Han Xin road.
idiomatic: In the province he memorialized on Tongling road and the old Han Xin road.

literal: Also east of the province by the sea he raised a long dike, blocking salt tide without and channeling fresh water within.
idiomatic: East of the province along the coast he also raised a long dike, holding back the salt tide outside and drawing fresh water within.

literal: Edicts approved all and were carried out.
idiomatic: Edicts approved all of it and it was carried out.

literal: Transferred to inspector of Xuzhou; before taking office, he was again made inspector of Jiaozhou.
idiomatic: He was transferred to inspector of Xuzhou; before he took up the post he was again made inspector of Jiaozhou.

literal: Bi was refined and tolerant, especially expert in the duties of historiography.
idiomatic: Bi was refined and forgiving, and above all skilled in the historian's craft.

literal: Wherever he served he was clean; officials and people cherished him.
idiomatic: Wherever he served he kept things clean, and officials and common people held him dear.

literal: He loved the profundities of mystery; in old age he grew ever more devoted.
idiomatic: He loved the profundities of the dark learning; in old age he grew only more devoted.

literal: He also annotated the "Hui Shi" chapter of the Zhuangzi and the upper and lower appendices of the Changes, titled New Annotated Garden of Meanings, and both circulated in the world.
idiomatic: He also annotated the "Hui Shi" chapter of the Zhuangzi and the upper and lower appendices of the Changes, under the title New Annotated Garden of Meanings, and both circulated in his day.

literal: Bi's nature was upright; in the hegemonic court era he often corrected matters.
idiomatic: Bi's nature was straight; in the hegemonic court he often set things right.

literal: When Xianzu became chancellor and reached the head of the staff, on first hearing talk of yielding the throne he still offered remonstrance.
idiomatic: When Gao Yang became chancellor and rose to head the staff, on first hearing talk of yielding the throne he still spoke against it.

literal: Xianzu once asked Bi, "In governing a state, whom should one employ?"
idiomatic: Gao Yang once asked Bi, "In governing a state, whom should one employ?"

literal: He replied, "For Xianbei chariot-and-horse guests, one still must use Chinese men."
idiomatic: He replied, "For Xianbei chariot-and-horse men, one still must use Chinese men."

literal: Xianzu took this speech as mocking him.
idiomatic: Gao Yang took this as a jibe at himself.

literal: Gao Dezheng held a key post and could not put up with him; before the crowd he openly rebuked him, saying, "Yellow Gate attendants are at the emperor's side — how can they hear what is good and not be startled, and only love to cut, trim, and suppress!"
idiomatic: Gao Dezheng held a key post and could not bring himself below Bi; before the assembly he openly rebuked him: "Yellow Gate men stand at the emperor's side — how can they hear what is good and not be stirred, and only love to pare away and crush?"

literal: Dezheng bore deep resentment and many times spoke of his faults.
idiomatic: Dezheng nursed deep hatred and spoke of his faults again and again.

literal: He also had chief secretary Du Yongzhen secretly report that during Bi's days as chief clerk he accepted entreaties and on a great scale arranged marriage festivities.
idiomatic: He also had chief secretary Du Yongzhen secretly report that in Bi's days as chief clerk he took bribes and on a great scale staged marriage festivities.

literal: Xianzu harbored it inwardly.
idiomatic: Gao Yang nursed it inwardly.

literal: Bi, relying on old ties, still made official requests on public business.
idiomatic: Bi, trusting in old ties, still pressed official requests.

literal: In the summer of the tenth year, the emperor, while drinking, accumulated his faults and sent orders to execute him at the province; he was sixty-nine at the time.
idiomatic: In the summer of the tenth year the emperor, while drinking, piled up his faults and sent orders to execute him in his province; he was sixty-nine.

literal: Soon he regretted it and sent couriers in pursuit, but they could not overtake.
idiomatic: Soon he regretted it and sent couriers in pursuit, but they could not catch up.

literal: His eldest son Rui and fourth son Guang were exiled far to Linhai garrison.
idiomatic: His eldest son Rui and fourth son Guang were exiled far to Linhai garrison.

literal: His second son Taiqing had already been exiled to Eastern Yuzhou.
idiomatic: His second son Taiqing had already been exiled to Eastern Yuzhou.

literal: At the beginning of Ganming they were all allowed to return to Ye.
idiomatic: At the opening of Ganming they were all allowed to return to Ye.

literal: In the fifth year of Tiantong he was posthumously enfeoffed with Bi as Bearer of the Staff, military commander of Yang and E provinces, Grand Master Equal in Rank to the Three Dukes, Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and inspector of Yang Province, with posthumous title Wen Su.
idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tiantong, Bi was posthumously given bearer of the staff, command of Yang and E provinces, grand master equal in rank to the three dukes, right vice director of the masters of writing, and inspector of Yang Province, with posthumous title Wen Su.

literal: Rui and Taiqing both had learning.
idiomatic: Rui and Taiqing both had learning.

literal: Taiqing's literary brush was especially skilled and he was praised in his age.
idiomatic: Taiqing's brush was especially fine, and his own age praised him.

literal: Rui, styled Zimei, in Wuping was vice director of the Court of Judicature and concurrent regular attendant, and chief of the mission to Chen.
idiomatic: Rui, styled Zimei, in Wuping was vice director of the court of judicature and concurrent regular attendant, and headed the mission to Chen.

literal: In his later years he was a langzhong in the Ministry of Personnel.
idiomatic: In his later years he was a langzhong in the ministry of personnel.

literal: Under Sui Kaihuang he ended his days as inspector of Kai Province.
idiomatic: Under Sui Kaihuang he ended his days as inspector of Kai Province.

literal: Taiqing, styled Shaoshan, served in succession as secretariat and Yellow Gate vice director, and concurrently as grand author and compiler of the national history.
idiomatic: Taiqing, styled Shaoshan, served in turn as secretariat and Yellow Gate vice director, and concurrently as grand author and compiler of the national history.

literal: At the end of Wuping he was libationer of the Imperial University and concurrently held the post of left vice director in the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: At the end of Wuping he was libationer of the imperial university and concurrently left vice director in the masters of writing.

literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, he ordered eighteen noted court scholars from Yang Xiuzhi, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, downward to follow the imperial train into Guan; the Rui brothers were not among those named.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, he ordered eighteen noted court scholars from Yang Xiuzhi, left vice director of the masters of writing, downward to follow the train into Guan; the Rui brothers were not on the list.

literal: Taiqing was later summoned, but because of deafness he was released and sent home.
idiomatic: Taiqing was later summoned, but because of deafness he was released and sent home.

literal: Under Sui Kaihuang he was summoned as author in the Masters of Writing; after a little more than a year, on account of age he retired from office, and an edict permitted it.
idiomatic: Under Sui Kaihuang he was summoned as author in the masters of writing; after a little more than a year, on account of age he retired, and an edict allowed it.

literal: His rites were especially favored; salary was granted for life, and before long he died.
idiomatic: His rites were especially favored; salary was granted for life, and before long he died.

literal: The historian writes: Sun Qian was at the prince's convenient side in a place of brush and ink; he had entered the staff not long, yet bonds were already deep.
idiomatic: The historian writes: Sun Qian stood at the prince's side in the place of brush and ink; he had entered the staff not long, yet affection was already deep.

literal: When he suddenly died, the Grand Ancestor said he had broken his right arm — though military banners had not yet been rolled up, he cherished talented men; otherwise how could one achieve hegemonic enterprise.
idiomatic: When he suddenly died, Gao Huan said he had broken his right arm — though the banners of war had not yet been furled, he cherished men of talent; otherwise how could one achieve a hegemon's work.

literal: The Grand Historian said: "It is not dying that is hard; it is facing death that is hard."
idiomatic: The Grand Historian said: "It is not dying that is hard; it is facing death that is hard."

literal: "Some weigh heavier than Mount Tai; some are lighter than a goose feather."
idiomatic: "Some weigh heavier than Mount Tai; some are lighter than a goose feather."

literal: This is the meaning.
idiomatic: Such is the meaning.

literal: Yuankang, with intelligence and talent, entrusted himself to the hegemonic court, intimate in the tent, with weighty trust.
idiomatic: Yuankang, with intelligence and talent, gave himself to the hegemonic court, intimate in the command tent, with weighty trust.

literal: At the difficulty he did not seek escape; he forgot life and followed righteousness — one may say he found his place.
idiomatic: At the crisis he did not seek escape; he forgot life and followed righteousness — one may say he met his place.

literal: Yang Yin considered himself of unusual conduct and peerless talent above the barbarian ranks; at the time of regicide he rushed to flee — so it is not that facing death is hard; dying is also hard.
idiomatic: Yang Yin thought himself of unusual conduct and talent above the barbarian ranks; at the regicide he rushed to flee — so it is not that facing death is hard; dying is hard too.

literal: Xianzu in youth concealed his talent; no court minister knew him. At the crisis of the Northern Palace, by order of age he was pressed forward — therefore the succession was not yet accepted at the time.
idiomatic: Gao Yang in youth concealed his gifts; no court minister knew him. At the crisis of the Northern Palace, by order of age he was pressed forward — so the succession was not yet accepted at the time.

literal: Du Bi's learning was discerning and clear; his speech was upright counsel. At the abdication transition he first raised dissenting views.
idiomatic: Du Bi's learning was discerning and clear; his speech was upright counsel. At the abdication he was first to raise a different plan.

literal: The king's anger had not yet subsided when he at last suffered manifest execution.
idiomatic: The king's anger had not yet cooled when he at last suffered open execution.

literal: Straight words were many — could one avoid reaching this?
idiomatic: Straight words were many — who could avoid coming to this?

literal: The encomium says: Yanjun galloping — talent high, conduct crooked.
idiomatic: The encomium says: Yanjun galloping — talent high, conduct crooked.

literal: Yuankang loyal and brave — he gave up life and kept righteousness.
idiomatic: Yuankang loyal and brave — he gave up life and kept righteousness.

literal: Lofty Fuxuan — thought reached talk of heaven; the Way perished, the times dark; body destroyed, name whole.
idiomatic: Lofty Fuxuan — thought reached talk of heaven; the Way was lost, the times dark; body destroyed, name whole.

literal: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
